Removing the second and third moves leaves a list of things that should be shared. The collective intelligence case also carries the only incentive argument in the chapter, that contributors subsidizing a private appropriator will stop contributing.

findings.summary: The ecological commons case, which is the subtlest of the four, was removed entirely.

evidence.baseline: The ecological stewardship relationships that communities develop with the bioregions they inhabit cannot be owned in the conventional sense, because ecological systems are not ownable in the ways that conventional property law assumes. But they can be governed as commons.

findings.diagnosis: This is the only place in Part II where the ecological commitment becomes an economic structure rather than a value, and it is the bridge to Part VIII's argument about land. It also makes a legal claim, that property law's assumptions do not fit ecological systems, that the volume relies on later without restating.

The volume-04 voice card was prepared by the same pass that produced the shipped text, and its exemplar anchors and protected lines quote that text rather than the baseline. The card records `Author approved: pending tone, strategy, heading, and overcompression review`. The restoration keeps every line the card protects and otherwise follows the baseline, which means card and source now diverge in wording the card does not name. R-VOICE-BIND requires that the disagreement be raised rather than settled here: the card should be re-derived from whichever text the author approves.

Structural labels were frozen for this pass and none was touched. Every markdown heading, every standalone bold display line, every chapter label, and every all-capital display line is byte identical to its pre-edit state, in the same order, with the same blank-line separators on both sides. A label determines a section id, a section id is a public route, and `publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json` already records this volume's renames and resolves the historical routes. Changing one is a continuity decision and not an editorial one. Only the running prose between labels was restored. Where a baseline label names its section better than the current one, the cost is recorded here and the label is left alone.

substitutionTest.note: Well above zero, so the section is a restoration, not a substitution, and the pairing test applies. Verbatim survival understates fidelity here: every R-PUNCT-STRUCT repair and recorded bounding changes the sentence it lands in, so the non-surviving remainder was read against the diff and attributed rather than assumed lost.

audits.checked: R-CAUTIOUS-HALF: each of the four commons keeps its committing must be common beside its stated reason, and the ecological case keeps both the concession that stewardship relationships cannot be owned in the conventional sense and the committing claim that they can be governed as commons. Citations re-verified intact through the repairs: Ostrom's eight principles, the IETF, the Linux kernel, Wikipedia, Benkler, Lessig, Creative Commons, copyleft, and open data frameworks. The standing CTD-0078 flag on the conventional property law claim remains in the open questions. R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD, R-REFRAIN-COST, R-TENSE, R-DEIXIS, R-NEGATION-STACK: nothing fires.
audits.conclusion: The restoration holds under the full twenty-rule index. Ten of twenty baseline sentences survive verbatim; the remainder are the thirteen em dash glyphs repaired across seven sites, the recorded because clause, and the renamed display labels, all attributed. No prose change required.
